clue.text: Refuse to arrange a bed for the night

definitions.meaning: to reject or decline an offer

definitions.text: arrange a bed for the night
definitions.meaning: hotel staff fold back the covers of a bed ready for the guest at night

explanation.definitionFit: To reject an offer is to decline it, and a hotel maid folds back bedclothes in the evening service of that name.

clue.text: Island race holding article over for military display

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the TT is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a is the indefinite article
too means over, excessively

explanation.surface: An island motor race including a newspaper piece about an army show.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man. 'holding' puts A inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening military performance of music and marching, like Edinburgh's, is a ceremonial show by troops.

clue.text: Outstanding judge about to tell a story

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, around, the second

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a game
to tell a story is to lie

explanation.surface: A remarkable judge is on the point of narrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' only links. A carving in raised relief stands out from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Carving that stands out from its background is said to be in raised projection, literally standing out.

clue.text: Not what is meant by fallen women!

definitions.text: Not what is meant by fallen women!

parts.words: Not what is meant by fallen women!
parts.note: a phrase for those who have fallen out of society, literally ones who fell, but who are not the immoral women of Victorian speech

explanation.definitionFit: People who abandon school or conventional life are said to have quit, which a literal reading makes into falling.

clue.text: Little kids start some time

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Small children begin at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little kids' looks like one phrase for children, but splits as WEE and the first letter of 'kids'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days is a period of time, so it is some time.

clue.text: Allow a couple of hundred — or five hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them give CC
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone haggling over whether to permit two hundred or five hundred of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like amounts being allowed, but they are Roman numerals: two Cs and a D, with the clue's own A and OR between.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant or concede something to someone is to allow it, as in according them respect.

clue.text: Cheats can appear decent

indicators.note: the letters can show up in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even cheats may seem respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and modest in conduct, especially sexually, is virtuous, so decent.

clue.text: It's not in Conservatives to be radical

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the political right means conservatives

explanation.surface: Being excluded from the Tory party makes one extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and thoroughgoing, as in an outright ban, so radical rather than partial.

clue.text: A beast framing evidence -a scheming fellow

indicators.note: one piece frames, surrounds, the other

parts.note: a deer is a beast
a sign is evidence of something

explanation.surface: A brute fabricating evidence is a crafty man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing evidence' suggests planting false proof, but DEER frames (surrounds) SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with designs is a plotter, so a man with schemes.

clue.text: Argue the pros and cons when it's time for action?

definitions.meaning: to discuss a matter thoroughly before deciding
read literally, the phrase says the chatter is finished, so now one must act

explanation.definitionFit: Discussing something thoroughly is debating it, and split as two words it says the debating is finished and deeds must follow.

clue.text: A six-footer may have stamina without a work-out

indicators.note: a work-out exercises and reshapes, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word a is to be taken away from the word stamina

explanation.surface: An athletic person of six feet might have endurance even without training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes one A from STAMINA, and 'work-out' rearranges the remaining STMINA. 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect has six legs, so the praying insect of that name is literally a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Supervisor in favour of call-up

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to name is to call

explanation.surface: A supervisor in support of military conscription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' looks like military conscription, but splits into two jobs: the synonym and, in a down clue, the upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The worker in charge of a crew or factory floor oversees the others, so a supervisor.

clue.text: Top man bearing a great deal from a catty creature

parts.note: OC is officer commanding, the man at the top of a unit
E, east, is a compass bearing
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A commander carrying a large amount away from a spiteful creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like 'carrying', but it is a compass bearing, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted wild cat of the Americas is a feline, hence a catty creature.

clue.text: Having no liking for the record with a poor content

indicators.note: the contents of something sit inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of a ship's voyage
thin means poor, as in a thin excuse

explanation.surface: Someone disliking a recording whose substance is weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the satisfied adjective, but is read as 'contents', the stuff held inside the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Detesting something means having a strong aversion to it, the opposite of fondness.

clue.text: Support a co-worker as permitted by society

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
an ally works with you

explanation.surface: Backing a colleague as society allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Done lawfully means done within the law, so as society permits.

clue.text: Broadcast made by a high minded individual about to marry

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a person of lofty thoughts
re is Latin for 'concerning', about
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A programme put out by an idealistic person on the point of marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio or TV, but it is the old farming sense: scattered seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered widely, as seed is sown by hand, the past tense of strew.

clue.text: There's something afoot — the woman accepts …

indicators.note: the pronoun takes in another letter, as a host accepts a guest

parts.note: she refers to a woman
the ellipsis points on to the next clue, whose answer is the tennis word for a nil score, and nil is the letter O

explanation.surface: Something is going on: the woman agrees to what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, whose answer is a tennis score of nothing; that nothing is O, which SHE takes in. 'Afoot' suggests something happening, but means literally on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is worn on the foot, so it is literally an item that is on a foot.

clue.text: The trumpeter from Nepal — the composer

indicators.note: a composer puts notes in order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A musician from Nepal, and the man who wrote the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The trumpeter' and 'composer' suggest musicians; the trumpeter is the beast that trumpets, and NEPAL THE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This large animal trumpets through its trunk, so it is a trumpeter.

clue.text: Be pressing about a certain wild animal

parts.note: over means about, as in talk over
a bear is a wild animal

explanation.surface: Be insistent about some wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate overbearingly is to be domineering or pushy, so pressing.

clue.text: Put out, rate evil member of the family

indicators.note: putting something out of order rearranges it

explanation.surface: Annoyed, I rate a wicked relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like annoyed but rearranges RATE EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman or kinswoman is someone related to you, so of the family.

clue.text: … this without point

parts.note: in tennis the score for a player with no points at all, linked from the previous clue

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring the word for zero is used for a player who has won no points.

clue.text: The boss of a German organisation

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking who runs a German company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like a company but tells you to rearrange the letters of A GERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of a business or team is its head, the one who runs it.

clue.text: Comparison which can make one break out into a grin

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the other word, going inside it

parts.note: a grin is a smile
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A comparison that might make someone burst into a grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break out into a grin' reads as an idiom, but I (one) goes into SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech comparing two things with 'like' or 'as' is a stated comparison.

clue.text: Wreck in a spot much used by sailing folk

definitions.text: spot much used by sailing folk

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, wreck

explanation.surface: A shipwreck at a place popular with yachtsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' suggests a shipwreck, but is the verb MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour with moorings for yachts is a place yachtsmen use.

clue.text: Written when incarcerated?

definitions.meaning: shut in a pen, an enclosure, like a prisoner

explanation.definitionFit: Words composed with a pen are written, and animals shut in a pen are confined like prisoners.

clue.text: A piece of journalistic writing on parking

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
an article is a piece written for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper column about car parking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'piece of journalistic writing' as one phrase, but 'A piece' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bit or fragment of something is a speck, a small piece of it.

clue.text: An artist may go into a bistro just for a bottle

indicators.note: one piece is said to enter the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cafe is a small informal restaurant like a bistro
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter visits a bistro simply to get a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: RA goes inside CAFE. RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy, a British art institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass flask for serving wine or water at table is a type of bottle.

clue.text: A wearisome guy, sound but such a swine

indicators.note: the clue says the word is spoken, so it sounds like another spelling

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A tiresome man, healthy but a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but signals a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A male pig, wild or domestic, is a swine.

clue.text: One little jerk is really sour

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A man calls an irritating person a real sourpuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests an unpleasant person, but here it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes vinegar's acid, so it means intensely sour.

clue.text: Act before an underling gains control

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: to do is to act
a minion is a servile underling

explanation.surface: Moving before a subordinate seizes power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereignty or authority over a territory is rule, the power to govern.

clue.text: Dealing with others' distress

indicators.note: dealing as with cards deals the letters out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Coping with the suffering of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing with' reads as coping, but deals out (rearranges) the letters of OTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent pangs or a hard struggle, as in death's agonies, mean anguish or suffering.

clue.text: A way of drawing complimentary applause

parts.note: complimentary tickets are free of charge
to give someone a hand is to applaud them

explanation.surface: A style of sketching that earns flattering clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complimentary' seems to mean flattering, matching the applause, but means given at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching without a ruler or compass is the unaided manner of drawing by hand alone.
